issues.description: filters='*.exe' breaks the file picker on Linux and macOS where conda binaries have no extension
issues.detail: The browse dialog restricts selection to *.exe, a Windows-only convention. On Linux and macOS, conda/mamba/micromamba are extensionless and will be invisible in the picker, forcing users to type the path. Make the filter platform-conditional or drop it; validate_conda already enforces correctness.

issues.description: validate_conda substring match accepts any binary whose --version output contains 'conda' or 'mamba'
issues.detail: `any(tool in out.decode().lower() ...)` matches the substring anywhere in the output, so 'not-conda' or 'mambo-clone v1' passes. Anchor on the leading token of the version string with a regex like `^(conda|mamba|micromamba)\s+\d` to validate the identifying tool name and version.

issues.description: out.decode() without encoding/errors handling can crash on non-UTF-8 locales and stderr is ignored
issues.detail: run_program returns bytes; default decoding can raise UnicodeDecodeError on Windows code pages, silently rejecting a valid conda via the bare except. Additionally, some conda variants print --version to stderr, which is discarded. Capture both streams and decode with errors='replace'.

issues.description: validate_conda complects existence, executability, subprocess probe, and identity-matching in one predicate
issues.detail: The function answers four questions at once and treats empty-string as valid as a fifth. A caller cannot ask any one in isolation. Decompose into a pure predicate over the stdout string and a small effectful probe, and add a timeout to communicate() so a hung binary cannot freeze the preferences UI.

issues.description: custom_conda boolean and conda_path string model one fact in two places, and resolution is inlined in argv()
issues.detail: 'Which conda to use' is split across a flag and a path that only matters when the flag is true, and argv() inlines find_conda + two config lookups to resolve it. Worse, a user-set conda_path is ignored when find_conda succeeds, contradicting the override intent. Extract resolve_conda_executable() and let the custom path take precedence.

issues.description: Custom-conda combination is not validated on apply; empty path with checkbox enabled silently falls through
issues.detail: The checkbox only toggles widget enablement; nothing clears conda_path on uncheck or requires a non-empty existing path when checked. A user can enable custom_conda, leave the field blank, save, and only discover the failure at kernel start. Validate the combination on apply and document the empty-string-is-accepted shortcut in validate_conda's docstring.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the feature is well-shaped — let users point Spyder at a conda binary when auto-detection fails — but the implementation has several concrete defects. validate_conda is the main hotspot: substring matching on --version output, naive decoding without encoding/errors handling, no timeout, and four orthogonal checks braided into one predicate. The Windows-only *.exe filter silently breaks the file picker on Linux and macOS. Configuration models one fact as two values, resolution logic is inlined in argv() and silently ignores the user's explicit override when auto-detection succeeds, and the checkbox/path combination is not validated on apply.
